Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verses 1–2:

Tafsir of Surat al-Haqqah

It is Meccan.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his book, with his chain of narration, that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I encountered the Messenger of Allah before I embraced Islam. I went to the mosque and found that he had preceded me to it, and he had stood to pray, so I stood behind him. He recited Surat al-Haqqah, and I began to marvel at the composition of the Qur'an, and I said: 'He is a poet, as the Quraysh say.' Until he reached the words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger. It is not the word of a poet﴾ to the end of the surah. Then I knew that he was not a poet, and Islam settled in my heart."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿The Inevitable Reality. What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ "al-Haqqah" is a name for the Resurrection (al-qiyamah).

The Resurrection was called al-haqqah because in it the realities of matters (ḥawāqq al-umūr) appear, that is, their true natures (haqāʾiquhā).

It is also said: it was so called because it establishes (ḥaqqqat) upon every person his deeds, whether good or evil, and manifests its recompense of reward and punishment.

Al-Azhari said: It was called al-haqqah because it confronts (tuḥiqqu) the disbelievers who disputed with the prophets in this world, denying it.

The Arabs say: "ḥāqaqtu fulānan fa-ḥaqqaqtuhu," meaning: I disputed with so-and-so and overcame him in the dispute.

His words ﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ are mentioned in the manner of magnification and exaltation.

Imru' al-Qays said:

(Leave aside the plunder that was cried out about in its pastures... rather, the tale is what the tale of the riding-camels is.)

Here "mā" is an interrogative, and it is mentioned in this place to magnify the matter of the riding-camels.

Likewise here.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Everywhere He says "adraka" (what will make you know), He has informed the Prophet (ﷺ), and where He says "wa-ma yudrika" (and what will make you know), He has not informed him.

It is also mentioned in the manner of magnification and emphasis.

Similar to this is the verse of Abu al-Najm in poetry:

(I am Abu al-Najm, and my poetry is my poetry...)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity﴾. "Al-Qari'a" is also a name for the Resurrection.

Al-Mubarrad said: The Resurrection was named "al-Qari'a" because it strikes the hearts and bursts upon them with severity and distress.

And His saying: ﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast⁠﴾. Mujahid said: "By their transgression," and this is also the view of Abu 'Ubayda.

It is said: "By the overwhelming (al-ṭāghiya)," meaning: by the cry (al-ṣayḥa).

And it is said: by the quake (al-rajfa).

The cry was named ṭāghiya because it exceeded the measure that hearing can bear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿But as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a furious wind, violently cold﴾. That is, it was a wind of intense cold.

On this view, it is derived from ṣirr (ṣarr), which means cold.

It was also said: [it was] a wind with a loud cry (ṣayḥah).

On this view, it is derived from ṣarrah, which is the loud cry.

And His saying ﴿raging (ʿātiyah)﴾: that is, it rebelled against its keepers (khazanah).

Qabīṣah ibn Dhu’ayb said:

Allah did not send any wind except in a known measure, other than the wind which He sent upon ʿĀd, for it went forth without a known measure, in anger at the wrath of Allah, exalted is He.

This was also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.

It is said: this wind was named ʿātiyah because it exceeded the measure.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿He subjected them to it﴾, meaning: He let it loose and sent it against them, ﴿seven nights and eight days, in succession﴾, meaning: consecutive.

It is said: "Ominous."

It is also said: He named it ḥusūm (ḥusūm, "exterminating") because it killed them and annihilated them, from al-ḥasm, which is cutting off.

In the tafsir it is related that its beginning was from the morning of Wednesday, and it is said: from the morning of Sunday.

And His saying ﴿you would see the people in it laid low﴾, meaning: they were struck down and became ﴿as if they were trunks of hollow palm trees﴾, meaning: roots of palm trees cut off from their places.

﴿Hollow﴾: al-Azharī said: He named it "hollow" because when they are uprooted their places are emptied of them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 8:

And His words, ﴿So do you see any remnant of them?﴾ meaning: any surviving soul.

It is also said: any survival.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾. It is also read "wa man qablahu" (and those before him), meaning: the nations that were before him.

And His saying: ﴿and the overturned cities﴾ are the towns of Lot.

Accordingly, its meaning is: and the people of the overturned cities.

It was also said: "al-Mu'tafikat" (the overturned cities) are the people of Lot, because he (the city) was overturned with them (ā'tafaka bihim).

And His saying: ﴿with the sin﴾ means: with the great error, that is, with the great sin.

And His saying: ﴿So they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, and He seized them with a severe seizing﴾. That is: an increased seizing, exceeding the other seizings.

It is also said: the punishment was increased in proportion to their deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 11:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿When the water overflowed﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It became angry with the anger of God, and so it overflowed.

It is also said: taghā means: it exceeded the measure.

It is said that it rose above every thing in the world by five [cubits].

And it has been said that it was more than that.

And His words: ﴿We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ means: the ship (al-safinah), and its plural is al-jawari, and they are ships (al-sufun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 12:

And His saying: ﴿So that We might make it a reminder for you﴾, meaning: a lesson (ʿibrah) and an admonition (waʿẓah).

Qatadah said: The early members of this community encountered the ship of Noah, and how many ships have perished, but Allah the Exalted preserved this ship as a reminder for this community and a lesson for it.

It is also said: He made it a reminder for you, meaning: that you might remember this account, so that it becomes a lesson and an admonition for you and for whoever hears it.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that an attentive ear may retain it﴾, meaning: an ear that comprehends the command of Allah and acts upon it.

Makhul narrated that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him: "I asked Allah that He make it your ear."

ʿAli said: "After that, I never heard anything and then forgot it."

.

Divine saying: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown﴾. We have already explained the meaning of the Trumpet (al-Sur).

And His saying: ﴿a single blast﴾, meaning: the first blast.

And His saying: ﴿single﴾, meaning: it has no repetition (mathniyya) to it.

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And the earth and the mountains are lifted up and crushed with one blow⦆ — that is, they are shaken with one shaking.

It is also said: they are pulverized into one crumbling.

And it has been said: one of them strikes the other, so that both collapse and are destroyed.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿So on that Day the Inevitable will occur﴾ means: the Resurrection (qiyamah) came into being.

And His saying: ﴿And the heaven will be split open, for it that Day will be frail﴾, that is: weak.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: "It will be split open from the Milky Way (al-Majarra)."

It is said: "Shaqā wāh," meaning: weak and torn apart.

Among their proverbs:

(Leave the path of one whose cord has grown weak... and of one whose water has been spilled in the desert.)

It has also been said: ﴿fa-hiya yawma'idhin wāhiya﴾ means split open and torn apart, because that which grows weak is split and torn.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 69, verse 17:

And His saying: ﴿And the angels will be upon its sides﴾, meaning: upon its edges.

Al-Kisa'i said: upon its borders.

It was also said: upon the places of its cracks, looking down at the world.

And His saying: ﴿And there will bear the throne of your Lord above them that Day, eight﴾ — it was said: eight rows of angels.

In the Jami' of Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, with a narration from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was sitting among a company of his Companions when a cloud passed by. He said: "Do you know what this is called?" They said: "Yes, this is the clouds." The Messenger of Allah said: "The mizn?" They said: "And the mizn." The Messenger of Allah said: "And the 'inan?" They said: "And the 'inan." The Messenger of Allah said to them: "Do you know how far is the distance between the sky and the earth?" They said: "No, by Allah, we do not know." He said: "Indeed, the distance between them is either one, or two, or three and seventy years, and the sky above it is likewise, until he counted them as seven heavens."

He said: "Above the seventh heaven is a sea, between its upper and lower parts is the distance between one heaven and another. Above that are eight mountain goats (awʿal), between their hooves and their knees is the distance between one heaven and another. Then above their backs is the Throne, between its lowest and highest part is the distance between one heaven and another, and Allah is above that."

He (al-Sam'ani) said, may Allah be pleased with him: My father Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Sam'ani informed us of this; Abu al-'Abbas ibn Mahbub informed us; Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us; [ʿAbd ibn Humayd] informed us; ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays, from Simak ibn Harb, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmayra, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib... the report.

And in some reports: that among the bearers of the Throne is an angel in the form of a rooster, his feet are in the lowest depths of the earths and his head is beneath the Throne, and he has one wing in the east and one wing in the west. When he glorifies Allah, every thing glorifies Him along with him.

And al-Zuhri narrated from Anas that the Prophet said to Jibril: "I wish to see you in your true form." He said: "Indeed you cannot bear that." He said: "I would love for you to do it." He said: "So the Messenger of Allah went out to al-Batha', and Jibril showed him himself in the form in which Allah created him, with one wing in the east and one wing in the west, and his head in the sky. The Prophet fainted, then recovered, with his head in Jibril's lap, and Jibril had placed one of his hands on his chest and the other between his shoulders. Then he said: "If you had seen Israfil, who has twelve wings, and the Throne on his shoulder, and he sometimes shrinks out of fear of Allah until he becomes like a sparrow, [so that] he does not carry the Throne except by the majesty of Allah."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 18:

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿On that Day you will be exposed; not a secret of yours will be concealed﴾, meaning: no deed will be hidden, and the meaning is that nothing is hidden from Allah the Exalted.

It has been narrated from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "Take account of yourselves before you are called to account, weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and prepare yourselves for the greatest exposure."

And from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection there are three exposures: two are for disputation and excuses, and in the third, the books will be flown about."

This has also been narrated as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report.

And in some reports from ʿAʾisha, she said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you remember your families on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "As for three places, no: at the time the books are flown about, at the Scale, and at the Bridge (al-Sirat, the bridge over Hell)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 19:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: "Here, read my record!"﴾ That is: "Come, read my record!"

It is also said: it means "Take!"

The Arabs say to one person "hā'" (هاء), to two "hā'umā" (هاؤما), and to a group "hā'ū" (هاؤموا).

It has been narrated that a man called out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad!" So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hā'um" (هاؤم).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 20:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I was certain that I would encounter my account.﴾ That is: I was certain (ayqantu).

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Indeed, the believer had good expectation of Allah, so he did good deeds, and indeed the hypocrite had bad expectation of Allah, so he did evil deeds.

"And His saying, ﴿So he will be in a pleasing life﴾: meaning, one that has contentment (radiya, i.e. possessing satisfaction).

Abu 'Ubayda said: "Pleasing" (mardiyya), i.e. one with which he is pleased.

And it is said: "A pleasing life" is Paradise."
"And His saying: ﴿In a lofty garden﴾, meaning: elevated."

Concerning His the Exalted's words: ﴿Its fruits hanging low, within reach﴾. Al-Bara' ibn Azib said: "They take them while standing, sitting, and lying down," meaning, reclining.

And the meaning of "within reach" (daniyah) is: near to be taken, nothing preventing access to it by distance or thorns.

"And His saying: ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction for what you put forward in the days past﴾, meaning: what you sent ahead (qaddamtum), ﴿in the days past﴾, meaning: the bygone days, and these are in the world (al-dunya).

And it is related from some of them that the verse is about those who fast."
Allah's words: ﴿And as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: "Oh, would that I had not been given my record!"﴾ That is, "my record" (kitabi).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 26:

﴿And I did not know what my account was.﴾

That is: I did not expect my reckoning, because he would see no gain from his account, and would see everything against him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 27:

And His saying: ﴿Would that it had been the decisive end!﴾ That is: would that the death had been decisive, meaning: I would not have been revived after it, and it would have decreed for me annihilation forever.

It has also been said: "Would that it had been" means: would that I had died now.
"And His saying: ﴿Mā aghnā ʿannī māliyah﴾ — meaning: my wealth."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 29:

And His saying: ﴿My authority has perished from me﴾ means: my argument has been nullified, and my excuse was not heard. And it is only that it is not heard because he has no excuse.

And the sultan (ruler, authority) was named sultan because the proofs (ḥujaj) are established in his presence, or because he is a proof (ḥujjah) upon the creation, so that they may set their affairs in order.

Qatadah said: "It does not mean that he governs a village and collects its taxes, but rather he intended by it his authority over himself, since he squandered what God had granted him, committed sins, and neglected the commands."

.

The Lord's words, Most High: ﴿Seize him and shackle him﴾ means binding the hand to the neck.

It was also said: his foot is tied to his neck, and then he is dragged on his face.

Then the Blazing Fire: roast him (in it).

Wait, I need to render this accurately. The passage reads: "And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ﴾ i.e., ashwuhu." The Qur'anic quotation is ﴿ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ﴾, meaning "Then burn him in the Blazing Fire" (Q. 69:31). The gloss أي: اشوه means "i.e., roast/scorch him" in the sense of "ashwuhu," from شوى (to roast).

**Translation:**

And His saying: ﴿Then cast him into the Blazing Fire, roast him﴾, i.e., roast him (ashwuhu).

Then, into a chain whose length is seventy cubits. Nawf al-Bikali said: each cubit is seventy spans (bā'), and each span is from here to Mecca, and he was in Kufa at that time.

He narrated something similar to this from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

As for His saying (fasluku-hu), in the tafsir it is said: it enters into his mouth until it comes out from his posterior, and this is the meaning of His saying ﴿Then thread him﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty,﴾ ﴿nor did he urge the feeding of the needy.﴾ That is: he did not urge (others) to give.

Al-Hasan said: "I met people who would charge their families, when they went out, not to turn away any beggar. And I met people, one of whom would leave his brother in charge of his household for forty years."

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty,﴾ ﴿nor did he urge the feeding of the needy.﴾ That is: he did not urge (others) to give.

Al-Hasan said: "I met people who would charge their families, when they went out, not to turn away any beggar. And I met people, one of whom would leave his brother in charge of his household for forty years."

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿So today he has no close friend here﴾

Translation of the commentary:

And His saying: ﴿So today he has no close friend here﴾, meaning: a close relative (qarib).

And His saying: ﴿Nor any food except from ghislin﴾. Al-Ghislin: the pus of the people of the Fire.

It is related from al-Rabi' ibn Anas that he said: It is a tree that produces food, the most vile of the foods of the people of the Fire.

And in a report: a single bucket of ghislin, if it were poured out in this world, would make the people of this world stink.

And His saying: ﴿None eats it except the sinners﴾ — i.e., the polytheists.

It is also said: the people of disobedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 38:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So I swear by what you see﴾. That is: "I swear" (aqsimu), and "la" is a filler particle (silah).

Some have said that the meaning of "and what you do not see" (wa ma la tubsirun) is the angels.

In the tafsir it is said that the verse is a refutation of the polytheists, for some of them said, "Muhammad is a sorcerer (sahir)," and that was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and those who followed him. Some said, "He is a poet (shair)," and that was Abu Jahl and those who followed him. Some said, "He is a soothsayer (kahin)," and that was Uqba ibn Abi Mu'it and those who followed him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 40:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾, i.e., a noble messenger of Allah.

It has been said: it is Jibril (Gabriel).

It has been said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ).

If someone says: How did He say ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾, when it is in fact the word of Allah, exalted is He?

The answer has two aspects. The first: its meaning is the recitation of a noble messenger. The second: it is the word of Allah and the conveyance (iblagh) of a noble messenger. So the speech was expanded (ittasa'a fi al-kalam) and it sufficed with what is understood from the context (bi-al-fahwa).

And His saying: ﴿Nor is it the word of a poet; little do you believe.﴾ That is, you do not believe at all.

A man says to another: "Qalilan ma ta'tini" (you rarely come to me), meaning: you do not come to me at all.

And His words: ﴿nor the speech of a soothsayer﴾ The kahin (soothsayer) is one who reports about the unseen falsely.

It is also said: (he speaks) by conjecture and guesswork, not from knowledge.

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿Little is it that you take heed﴾, meaning: you do not take admonition at all, as we have explained.
And His saying: ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ — its meaning is apparent.
Allah's words: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings﴾ — meaning: that Muhammad, if he had attributed to Us some sayings, that is, said what We had not said.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 69, verse 45:

And His saying: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾, i.e., by force.

That is, We would have avenged Ourselves upon him by Our might and Our power. This is related from Mujahid. Al-Shammakh said:

(I saw ʿArabah al-Awsi striving toward good deeds, unmatched by any rival,)
(Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArabah meets it with the right hand.)

That is, with strength.

The historian said: His saying ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [means: by the truth]. It is also related from Thaʿlab, "by the truth."

This is also related from al-Suddi.

And from al-Hasan: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾, i.e., We would have taken away his strength.

It is said: ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ is like the saying of the speaker: "Take hold of his right hand" when he does something deserving punishment, i.e., by force.

And His saying: ﴿Then We would have cut off from him the aorta﴾, meaning: the tendon of the heart; when it is severed, the person does not live after it.

Al-Shammakh also said, addressing his she-camel:

(When you reach me and bear my saddle... at ʿArabah, then choke, with the blood of the aorta)

Its meaning: "And there is none of you who could hold Us back from him" (Q. 69:47).

[Meaning]: You attribute it to Me as a lie, but if I had seized him, none of you could have prevented Us from him.
And His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for the God-fearing﴾, i.e., the Qur'an.
And His saying: ﴿And indeed We know that among you are those who deny﴾, i.e., deny the Qur'an and the Messenger.
And His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a regret for the disbelievers﴾, i.e., the Resurrection is a regret for the disbelievers.
And His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth of certainty﴾ — meaning: the Resurrection is pure certainty and the very essence of certainty.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty.﴾ (Surah al-Haqqah 69:52)

Al-Sam'ani said: His words, ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾, mean: declare your Lord, the Mighty, free of all imperfection, and mention Him by His praiseworthy and fitting attributes.

In it there is evidence that the ism (name) is the musamma (the named), and that there is no difference between the two.
